headline: Trump: deportations 'too tough'. ICE: not slowing down.
summary: Trump told 60 Minutes on Sunday that his deportation policy 'might have been too tough' and 'both helped and hurt' his party in the midterms. The same day the White House told the BBC it will not slow down, and Homeland Security said ICE is 'NOT backing away'. ICE has been told to aim for 2,700 arrests a day, up from 2,000.

cover_question.q: Will they have to stop now?

cover_answer: No. His own team says ICE is not slowing down.
table_question: Can you say sorry for a rule and keep the rule?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: The president has been sending people who came to the US without permission back to their own countries. On TV Sunday he said maybe he was too tough about it, but his helpers said nothing changes. It's like a teacher calling a rule too strict and keeping it anyway. The grown-ups are sorting it out.
5-7.why: The teacher carries it, and the arrest count stays off the card. At six the picture is the story.
5-7.why_long: A six-year-old reasons from what is in front of them, so the script hands them one picture, a teacher who calls a rule too strict and keeps it, and leaves out the arrest target and the protests. Expect 'could they send someone I know away?' Answer from your own street, and say the plan did not change.

8-12.script: Trump's government has been deporting people in the US illegally, and ICE aims for 2,700 arrests a day. His party lost Congress, and Sunday he said the policy 'might have been too tough'. The same day the White House said it won't slow down: a thermostat set to 2,700, untouched.
8-12.why: Policy, election, admission, no change: a chain they can check at eleven.
8-12.why_long: Between eight and twelve a child checks whether adults apply their own rules, so the script hands them a chain to test: a policy, an election lost, a president calling it too tough, a target left at 2,700. The thermostat is the mechanism. Expect 'so was he lying?' Both were said on one day. ICE's next move is the answer.

13-17.script: Does 'might have been too tough' change anything if the arrest target stays at 2,700 a day? Trump said it on 60 Minutes Sunday; the same day his spokeswoman said no president has been stronger on enforcement. Second: Vance is open to going after employers instead. Softer, or different?
13-17.why: Interview against statement, same day. At fifteen they can hold both.
13-17.why_long: A teenager can hold two true things at once, so the script puts the 60 Minutes answer next to the spokeswoman's statement from the same Sunday and asks which is the policy. Argument is a skill practised on you. Expect 'so he admitted he was wrong?' Not quite. He said it both helped and hurt, and the target stayed put.

5-7.q: Will they have to stop now?
5-7.a: No. The people in charge say the plan stays the same. The president only said it might have been too tough.

8-12.q: Why did he say it now?
8-12.a: His party lost Congress. Exit polls put immigration third for voters.
Not so far. The White House says no, and ICE's target is still 2,700 a day.

13-17.q: Why admit it if nothing changes?
13-17.a: He said it 'both helped and hurt'. A TV answer is not an order to ICE.

13-17.q: Who actually decides what ICE does?
13-17.a: The president. His new chief of staff, Stephen Miller, designed the policy.
